title: Narrative Systems Engineering: Signal-Grounded Multimodal Measurement and an Exploratory State-Space Model for Audiovisual Media
description:
Exploratory research program and C#/.NET multimodal software (Nse.Pipeline, Argon.Engine) originated by Jair Ivan Rojas Ruiz (ORCID: 0009-0003-1109-4583; foundational archive September 8, 2026).

What is measured: acoustic level and speech activity from PCM audio, visual change between sampled frames (Jensen-Shannon divergence of color distributions), luminance, saturation and color entropy, and transcript-based speech rate and lexical descriptors, all linked to exact time spans and source hashes.

What is proposed, not validated: composite indices (Narrative Energy, Entropy, Complexity, Inertia) whose weights and normalization constants are author-chosen and uncalibrated; stance vectors coded by a single coder without measured inter-annotator agreement; and an exploratory state-space model x(t+1) = f(x(t), u(t)) of belief dynamics that has not been compared with measured audience responses. Counterfactual montage results (EXP-003) are simulations of that model. EXP-004 recovers parameters from trajectories generated by the same model, which verifies the estimator but not the model.

Initial descriptive application to three short works (a 1994 Spanish university debate, the 1964 "Daisy" campaign spot, and the 1986 Challenger address). Three works are not sufficient to establish genre-level separation.

Other public uses of the phrase "Narrative Systems Engineering" exist; see docs/PRIOR_WORK_AND_DISAMBIGUATION.md.
